_meta.title: Indian GST — core provisions (illustrative demo corpus)
_meta.disclaimer: ILLUSTRATIVE summaries of real CGST/IGST Act 2017 provisions, written for a retrieval demo. Faithful to the statute but NOT verbatim bare-act text — verify against the official Act/Rules before any production or advice use.

provisions.title: Scope of supply
provisions.content: Supply includes all forms of supply of goods or services — sale, transfer, barter, exchange, licence, rental, lease or disposal — made or agreed to be made for a consideration in the course or furtherance of business. Schedule I lists activities treated as supply even without consideration (e.g. permanent transfer of business assets on which ITC was availed, supplies between related/distinct persons). Schedule III lists activities treated as neither supply of goods nor services (e.g. services by an employee to employer, sale of land).

provisions.title: Levy and collection (CGST)
provisions.content: CGST is levied on all intra-State supplies of goods or services (except alcoholic liquor for human consumption) on the value determined under s.15, at rates notified (0%, 5%, 12%, 18%, 28%), not exceeding 20%. s.9(3) empowers government to notify supplies taxed under reverse charge (recipient pays). s.9(5) makes e-commerce operators liable for specified services (e.g. passenger transport, restaurant services).

provisions.title: Levy and collection (IGST)
provisions.content: IGST is levied on all inter-State supplies of goods or services on the value under CGST s.15, at rates not exceeding 40%. IGST is also levied on imports of goods (as an additional duty of customs) and on import of services. Reverse-charge and e-commerce-operator provisions mirror CGST s.9(3)/(5).

provisions.title: Composition levy
provisions.content: A registered person whose aggregate turnover in the preceding FY did not exceed Rs 1.5 crore (Rs 75 lakh for special-category states) may opt to pay tax at a flat rate — 1% (traders), 5% (restaurants not serving alcohol), 6% (a supplier of services up to Rs 50 lakh under s.10(2A)). A composition dealer cannot collect tax from customers, cannot claim ITC, and cannot make inter-State outward supplies.

provisions.title: Time of supply of goods
provisions.content: The time of supply of goods is the earlier of (a) the date of issue of invoice (or the last date on which the invoice was required to be issued under s.31), or (b) the date of receipt of payment. For reverse-charge, it is the earliest of the date of receipt of goods, the date of payment, or the day after 30 days from the supplier's invoice date.

provisions.title: Time of supply of services
provisions.content: If the invoice is issued within the period prescribed under s.31 (30 days of supply of service), the time of supply is the earlier of the invoice date or the date of receipt of payment; if not issued in time, the earlier of the date of provision of service or the date of payment. For reverse-charge services, it is the earlier of the date of payment or the day after 60 days from the supplier's invoice date.

provisions.title: Value of taxable supply
provisions.content: The value of a supply is the transaction value — the price actually paid or payable — where the supplier and recipient are not related and price is the sole consideration. It includes any taxes/cesses (other than GST), incidental expenses (packing, commission), interest/late fees for delayed payment, and subsidies linked to price (except government subsidies). Discounts are excluded if recorded on the invoice, or if agreed before supply and linked to relevant invoices with ITC reversed by the recipient.

provisions.title: Eligibility and conditions for ITC
provisions.content: A registered person may take input tax credit on inward supplies used in the course or furtherance of business, subject to conditions: (i) possession of a tax invoice; (ii) the supply appears in the auto-populated GSTR-2B, i.e. the supplier furnished it (s.16(2)(aa)); (iii) receipt of the goods or services; (iv) the tax has actually been paid to government; and (v) the recipient has furnished the return under s.39. ITC for an invoice cannot be taken after 30 November following the end of the financial year, or the date of the annual return, whichever is earlier (s.16(4)).

provisions.title: Blocked credits
provisions.content: ITC is not available on certain inward supplies notwithstanding s.16, including: motor vehicles for transport of persons with seating capacity up to 13 (with exceptions); food and beverages, outdoor catering, health services, club/fitness memberships (unless used to make an outward taxable supply of the same category); works contract and construction of immovable property on own account; goods lost, stolen, destroyed or given as gifts/free samples; and tax paid under s.74, 129 and 130.

provisions.title: Persons liable for registration
provisions.content: A supplier must register in every State from which taxable supplies are made if aggregate turnover in a financial year exceeds the threshold: Rs 20 lakh for services (Rs 10 lakh in special-category states), and Rs 40 lakh for a supplier engaged exclusively in goods (subject to conditions). Aggregate turnover is computed PAN-India across all supplies.

provisions.title: Compulsory registration
provisions.content: Certain persons must register irrespective of turnover, including: persons making any inter-State taxable supply (of goods); casual and non-resident taxable persons; persons liable under reverse charge; e-commerce operators and persons supplying through them (with exceptions); persons required to deduct TDS (s.51) or collect TCS (s.52); and input service distributors.

provisions.title: Tax invoice
provisions.content: A registered person supplying taxable goods must issue a tax invoice before or at the time of removal/delivery; for services, within 30 days of supply (45 days for banks/NBFCs). The invoice must show the prescribed particulars — GSTIN of supplier and recipient, HSN/SAC, taxable value, and the CGST/SGST/IGST charged. A registered person supplying exempt goods/services or paying under composition issues a bill of supply instead.

provisions.title: Credit and debit notes
provisions.content: Where the taxable value or tax in an issued invoice exceeds the correct amount, or goods are returned or found deficient, the supplier issues a credit note; where it is less, a debit note. A credit note reducing output tax must be declared no later than 30 November following the financial year, and the recipient must correspondingly reverse ITC.

provisions.title: Payment of tax and order of ITC utilisation
provisions.content: Tax, interest and penalty are paid through the electronic cash ledger; output tax may be discharged using the electronic credit ledger (ITC). IGST credit must be fully utilised first, and only then may CGST and SGST/UTGST credit be used, in that order; CGST credit cannot be used to pay SGST and vice versa.

provisions.title: Inter-State supply
provisions.content: A supply is inter-State when the location of the supplier and the place of supply are in different States/UTs. Supplies to or from a Special Economic Zone, imports until they cross the customs frontier, and supplies in the taxable territory that are not intra-State are also treated as inter-State — and attract IGST.

provisions.title: Intra-State supply
provisions.content: A supply is intra-State when the location of the supplier and the place of supply are in the same State/UT — such a supply attracts CGST plus SGST/UTGST. Supplies to an SEZ, imports, and supplies to international tourists are expressly excluded from intra-State treatment.

provisions.title: Place of supply of goods (within India)
provisions.content: Where a supply involves movement of goods, the place of supply is the location where the movement terminates for delivery to the recipient. For 'bill-to ship-to' transactions, the place of supply is the principal place of business of the third person who directed the delivery. Where there is no movement, it is the location of the goods at delivery.

provisions.title: Place of supply of services (supplier & recipient in India)
provisions.content: The general rule: for a registered recipient the place of supply is the recipient's location; for an unregistered recipient it is the address on record, else the supplier's location. Specific rules override this — e.g. immovable-property services are taxed where the property is located, restaurant and personal-grooming services where performed, and passenger transport where the journey begins.

provisions.title: Place of supply where supplier or recipient is outside India
provisions.content: The default place of supply is the location of the recipient; where that is unavailable, the supplier's location. Exceptions include services relating to goods physically made available, immovable-property services, and admission to events — taxed where performed/located. This section governs export and import of services and OIDAR.

provisions.title: Zero-rated supply
provisions.content: Exports of goods or services and supplies to a Special Economic Zone developer/unit are zero-rated. A supplier may either export under a Letter of Undertaking (LUT) without paying IGST and claim a refund of unutilised ITC, or pay IGST on the export and claim a refund of the tax paid. Zero-rating preserves ITC even though the outward supply bears no tax.

provisions.title: Returns — GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B
provisions.content: s.37 requires the outward-supplies statement (GSTR-1) — invoice-level details of outward supplies. s.39 requires the monthly summary return and payment (GSTR-3B), where output tax and eligible ITC are declared and net tax paid. A return under s.39 cannot be furnished if any earlier return remains unfiled, and ITC in s.16 is conditional on filing.

provisions.title: Annual return (GSTR-9)
provisions.content: Every registered person (other than a few classes such as ISD, casual/non-resident taxable persons and TDS/TCS deductors) must file an annual return (GSTR-9) by 31 December following the financial year, with a self-certified reconciliation statement (GSTR-9C) where turnover exceeds the prescribed limit (currently Rs 5 crore).

provisions.title: E-invoicing (IRN)
provisions.content: Notified registered persons whose aggregate turnover exceeds Rs 5 crore in any financial year from 2017-18 onwards must generate invoices by reporting them to the Invoice Registration Portal, which returns a signed invoice with an Invoice Reference Number (IRN) and QR code. An invoice required to be so reported that is not is not treated as a valid tax invoice, and ITC to the recipient may be denied.

provisions.title: E-way bill
provisions.content: An e-way bill must be generated before movement of goods where the consignment value exceeds Rs 50,000, whether for supply, reasons other than supply, or inward supply from an unregistered person. It contains Part A (invoice and consignee details) and Part B (transporter/vehicle), and its validity depends on the distance to be covered.

provisions.title: GST rate slabs and HSN classification
provisions.content: GST rates are notified against HSN (goods) and SAC (services) codes, with principal slabs of 0% (exempt/nil), 5%, 12%, 18% and 28%, plus a compensation cess on certain demerit and luxury goods (e.g. tobacco, aerated drinks, some motor vehicles). Correct classification of the good or service to its HSN/SAC determines the applicable rate; most professional and IT services fall at 18%.
